claim: During apoptosis, Bcl-2 proteins such as Bax and Bak mediate the release of pro-apoptotic proteins from the mitochondria by clustering on the outer mitochondrial membrane and thereby permeabilizing it.
source: During apoptosis, Bcl-2 proteins such as Bax and Bak mediate the release of pro-apoptotic proteins from the mitochondria by clustering on the outer mitochondrial membrane and thereby permeabilizing it.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about the mechanism of apoptosis involving Bcl-2 family proteins.

claim: Bax clusters localize near outer membrane ruptures of highly variable size.
source: Our data show that Bax clusters localize near outer membrane ruptures of highly variable size.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations from the study's correlative microscopy and electron tomography data.

claim: Bax clusters contain structural elements suggesting a higher order organization of their components.
source: Bax clusters contain structural elements suggesting a higher order organization of their components.
evidence: This is based on structural observations from electron cryo-tomography data showing organized features within Bax clusters.

claim: Unfolding of inner membrane cristae is coupled to changes in the supramolecular assembly of ATP synthases.
source: Furthermore, unfolding of inner membrane cristae is coupled to changes in the supramolecular assembly of ATP synthases, particularly pronounced at membrane segments exposed to the cytosol by ruptures.
evidence: This claim is supported by observations of ATP synthase organization in electron tomography data of apoptotic mitochondria.

claim: Changes in ATP synthase assembly are particularly pronounced at membrane segments exposed to the cytosol by ruptures.
source: Furthermore, unfolding of inner membrane cristae is coupled to changes in the supramolecular assembly of ATP synthases, particularly pronounced at membrane segments exposed to the cytosol by ruptures.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of ATP synthase distribution in different regions of apoptotic mitochondria.

claim: Molecular reorganizations of the inner membrane and sequestration of outer membrane components into Bax clusters interplay in the formation of outer membrane ruptures.
source: Based on our results, we propose a comprehensive model in which molecular reorganizations of the inner membrane and sequestration of outer membrane components into Bax clusters interplay in the formation of outer membrane ruptures.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the integration of multiple experimental observations from the study.

claim: Pro-apoptotic members of the Bcl-2 protein family, including Bax, Bak, and Bok, are central to facilitating the release of apoptotic factors from the mitochondria into the cytosol.
source: Pro-apoptotic members of the Bcl-2 protein family, including Bax, Bak, and the less studied Bok, are central to facilitating the necessary release of apoptotic factors, such as cytochrome c and Smac/DIABLO, from the mitochondria into the cytosol (Jürgensmeier et al., 1998; Ke et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: In healthy cells, Bax cycles between the surface of mitochondria and the cytosol.
source: In healthy cells, Bax cycles between the surface of mitochondria and the cytosol, while Bak resides mostly on mitochondria (Edlich et al., 2011; Griffiths et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Bak resides mostly on mitochondria in healthy cells.
source: In healthy cells, Bax cycles between the surface of mitochondria and the cytosol, while Bak resides mostly on mitochondria (Edlich et al., 2011; Griffiths et al., 1999).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Upon activation by apoptotic stimuli, Bax/Bak stably inserts into the outer membrane of the mitochondria.
source: Upon activation by apoptotic stimuli, Bax/Bak stably inserts into the outer membrane of the mitochondria.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mechanism of Bax/Bak activation.

claim: Stable insertion of Bax/Bak into the outer membrane leads to permeabilization of the outer membrane, which is required for release of apoptotic factors from the intermembrane space.
source: This step leads to permeabilization of the outer membrane, which is required for release of the apoptotic factors from the intermembrane space, the compartment formed from the intracristae and peripheral space (Lovell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to previous research.

claim: Bax has been long known to form membrane pores and ruptures in vitro.
source: Bax has been long known to form membrane pores and ruptures in vitro (Antonsson et al., 1997; Basañez et al., 1999; Schafer et al., 2009; Schlesinger et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations to previous in vitro studies.

claim: In purified outer mitochondrial membranes, Bax-induced ruptures have been observed by electron cryo-microscopy.
source: In purified outer mitochondrial membranes, Bax-induced ruptures have been observed by electron cryo-microscopy (cryo-EM) (Gillies et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous cryo-EM study.

claim: Super-resolution fluorescence microscopy revealed that activated Bax forms rings devoid of outer mitochondrial membrane proteins, suggested to correspond to outer membrane ruptures several hundreds of nm in diameter.
source: Super-resolution fluorescence microscopy (FM) revealed that activated Bax forms rings devoid of outer mitochondrial membrane proteins, suggested to correspond to outer membrane ruptures several hundreds of nm in diameter (Große et al., 2016; Salvador-Gallego et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous super-resolution microscopy studies.

claim: The occurrence of large ruptures has been confirmed by electron cryo-tomography and associated with the extrusion of mitochondrial DNA through the opened outer membrane.
source: The occurrence of such large ruptures has been confirmed by electron cryo-tomography (cryo-ET), and associated with the extrusion of mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) through the opened outer membrane (McArthur et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous cryo-ET study.

claim: The ability of Bax/Bak to associate into oligomeric assemblies appears to be essential for permeabilizing the outer membrane.
source: While the mechanism of formation of these large ruptures remains elusive, the ability of Bax/Bak to associate into oligomeric assemblies appears to be essential for permeabilizing the outer membrane (Antonsson et al., 2000; Nechushtan et al., 2001; Westphal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on Bax/Bak oligomerization.

claim: The conformational changes that lead to Bax activation include insertion of a transmembrane helix into the outer membrane and subsequent dimerization of membrane-bound Bax.
source: The conformational changes that lead to Bax activation include insertion of a transmembrane helix into the outer membrane and subsequent dimerization of membrane-bound Bax (Bleicken et al., 2014; Brouwer et al., 2014; Czabotar et al., 2013; Dewson et al., 2008; Dewson et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous structural studies of Bax activation.

claim: Further accumulation of Bax into larger assemblies involves interactions via multiple, labile interfaces.
source: Further accumulation into larger Bax/Bak assemblies involves interactions via multiple, labile interfaces (Uren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study on Bax/Bak assembly.

claim: In fluorescence microscopy, the formation of Bax/Bak assemblies can be observed as small punctae on the mitochondria that coalesce into larger, mitochondria-associated cytosolic clusters that contain thousands of Bax/Bak molecules.
source: In FM, the formation of these assemblies can be observed as small punctae on the mitochondria that coalesce into larger, mitochondria-associated cytosolic clusters that contain thousands of Bax/Bak molecules (Nasu et al., 2016; Nechushtan et al., 2001; Zhou and Chang, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous fluorescence microscopy studies.

claim: Activation of Bax/Bak has been implicated in inner mitochondrial membrane rearrangements, suggested to be required for efficient discharge of apoptotic factors trapped in the intracristae space.
source: In addition to outer membrane rupturing, activation of Bax/Bak has been implicated in inner mitochondrial membrane rearrangements, suggested to be required for efficient discharge of apoptotic factors trapped in the intracristae space (Ban-Ishihara et al., 2013; Cipolat et al., 2006; Frezza et al., 2006; Scorrano et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies on inner membrane remodeling during apoptosis.

claim: Overexpression of Bax can induce cell death by apoptosis.
source: To mimic Bax-mediated apoptosis in HeLa cells, we took advantage of the previous observation that overexpression of Bax can induce cell death by apoptosis (Han et al., 1996; Pastorino et al., 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies showing that Bax overexpression induces apoptosis.

claim: When cells expressed cytosolic GFP-Bax in the presence of the caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh, GFP-Bax translocated to the mitochondria on average 77 min later (SD 69 min, N = 86 cells).
source: When cells expressed cytosolic GFP-Bax in the presence of the caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh, we observed on average 77 min later (SD 69 min, N = 86 cells) that GFP-Bax translocated to the mitochondria, which displayed fragmentation typical for apoptosis, as expected (Karbowski et al., 2002; Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from live-cell imaging experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Mitochondria displayed fragmentation typical for apoptosis upon GFP-Bax translocation.
source: When cells expressed cytosolic GFP-Bax in the presence of the caspase inhibitor Q-VD-OPh, we observed on average 77 min later (SD 69 min, N = 86 cells) that GFP-Bax translocated to the mitochondria, which displayed fragmentation typical for apoptosis, as expected (Karbowski et al., 2002; Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This observation is supported by the data shown in Figure 1 and is consistent with previous literature cited.

claim: On average 102 min (SD 57 min, N = 92 cells) after the initial recruitment into diffraction-limited punctae, larger, irregular foci of Bax appeared.
source: On average, 102 min (SD 57 min, N = 92 cells) after the initial recruitment into diffraction-limited punctae (Figure 1B), larger, irregular foci of Bax appeared (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from live-cell imaging experiments shown in Figure 1.

claim: Cells representing the two stages of Bax localization were similarly frequent 14–18 hr after GFP-Bax transfection.
source: Cells representing these two stages were similarly frequent 14–18 hr after GFP-Bax transfection.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental time course.

claim: Of 42 cells expressing GFP-Bax, 9 contained diffraction-limited Bax punctae and displayed no or little cytosolic cytochrome c release.
source: Of 42 cells expressing GFP-Bax, 9 contained diffraction-limited Bax punctae and displayed no or little cytosolic cytochrome c release (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Thirty-three cells contained larger GFP-Bax foci, of which 17 displayed partial and 16 complete cytochrome c release.
source: Thirty-three cells contained larger GFP-Bax foci, of which 17 displayed partial and 16 complete cytochrome c release (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C and D, respectively).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from immunofluorescence experiments shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Of 82 GFP-Bax signals targeted by electron tomography, 79 localized adjacent to mitochondria.
source: We targeted 82 GFP-Bax signals by ET and found that 79 of them localized adjacent to mitochondria (Figure 2; crosses).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from correlative microscopy experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Of the 82 GFP-Bax signals imaged, 77 localized to dense regions in the cytosol that were devoid of other cytosolic features and excluded ribosomes.
source: Further, of the 82 GFP-Bax signals imaged, 77 localized to dense regions in the cytosol that were devoid of other cytosolic features. In particular, they excluded the otherwise ubiquitously distributed ribosomes.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from electron tomography data.

claim: Ribosome-exclusion zones were irregular in shape and extended over approximately 100 to 1300 nm.
source: These regions were irregular in shape and extended over approximately 100 to 1300 nm.
evidence: This is a measurement from electron tomography data.

claim: More intense GFP-Bax signals corresponded to larger ribosome-exclusion zones.
source: More intense GFP-Bax signals corresponded to larger ribosome-exclusion zones (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an observation from correlative microscopy data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Ribosome-exclusion zones in the cytosol comprise the Bax clusters previously observed by immuno-electron, scanning confocal, and super-resolution microscopy.
source: We thus conclude that these ribosome-exclusion zones in the cytosol comprise the Bax clusters previously observed by immuno-electron, scanning confocal, and super-resolution microscopy (Große et al., 2016; Nasu et al., 2016; Nechushtan et al., 2001; Salvador-Gallego et al., 2016; Zhou and Chang, 2008).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the current data and comparison with previous studies cited.

claim: Mitochondria near GFP-Bax clusters often exhibited substantial gaps in their outer membranes (ruptures) that were between 100 and 700 nm wide (mean 316 nm, SD 156 nm, N = 37).
source: The mitochondria that we found near GFP-Bax clusters often exhibited substantial gaps in their outer membranes (Figure 2), which we henceforth refer to as ruptures. These ruptures were between 100 and 700 nm wide (mean 316 nm, SD 156 nm, N = 37).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Of the 37 mitochondrial ruptures found, 33 directly bordered the Bax clusters.
source: Of the 37 mitochondrial ruptures we found, 33 directly bordered the Bax clusters (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Near the rupture, the remaining outer membrane appeared associated with the inner membrane at a similar distance as in non-ruptured regions.
source: Near the rupture, the remaining outer membrane appeared associated with the inner membrane at a similar distance as in non-ruptured regions.
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography data.

claim: There were no outer membrane segments peeling off significantly from the inner membrane, or membrane segments loosely adhering to the remaining outer membrane.
source: There were no outer membrane segments peeling off significantly from the inner membrane, or membrane segments loosely adhering to the remaining outer membrane.
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography data.

claim: In 12 of the ruptured mitochondria, ribosome-like structures, often several dozen, were observed in the intermembrane space.
source: In 12 of the ruptured mitochondria, we observed ribosome-like structures, often several dozen, in the intermembrane space (Figure 2F and J; red circles and white spheres).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Ribosomes in the intermembrane space had leaked in from the cytosol through the outer membrane rupture.
source: As mitochondrial ribosomes are confined to the mitochondrial matrix, we concluded that these were ribosomes that had leaked in from the cytosol through the outer membrane rupture.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of ribosomes in the intermembrane space and knowledge of mitochondrial ribosome localization.

claim: 60 mitochondria near GFP-Bax clusters had ribosomes in the intermembrane space but had no outer membrane ruptures visible within the tomogram.
source: We also found 60 mitochondria near GFP-Bax clusters that had ribosomes in the intermembrane space, but that had no outer membrane ruptures visible within the tomogram (Figure 2H and L; red circles and white spheres).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The presence of ribosomes in the intermembrane space indicated that many of the mitochondria imaged had ruptures that were not contained within the imaged cell volume.
source: The ribosomes in the intermembrane space suggested that many of the mitochondria we imaged had ruptures that were not contained within the imaged cell volume.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of ribosomes in the intermembrane space without visible ruptures.

claim: Some ruptured mitochondria displayed canonical cristae folding.
source: The ruptured mitochondria in our dataset showed a wide heterogeneity of inner membrane morphology. While some ruptured mitochondria displayed canonical cristae folding (Figure 2E), others lacked cristae over large areas of a smooth inner membrane (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Some ruptured mitochondria lacked cristae over large areas of a smooth inner membrane.
source: The ruptured mitochondria in our dataset showed a wide heterogeneity of inner membrane morphology. While some ruptured mitochondria displayed canonical cristae folding (Figure 2E), others lacked cristae over large areas of a smooth inner membrane (Figure 2G and H).
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: More than one inner membrane compartment surrounded by a single outer membrane was frequently observed, indicating fragmentation of the inner membrane without concomitant outer membrane fission.
source: Furthermore, we frequently observed more than one inner membrane compartment surrounded by a single outer membrane, indicating fragmentation of the inner membrane without concomitant outer membrane fission.
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography data and an inference about inner membrane fragmentation.

claim: In cases of inner membrane fragmentation, one matrix displayed canonical cristae shape, while the other matrix lacked cristae.
source: In these cases, one matrix displayed canonical cristae shape, while the other matrix lacked cristae (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Bax activity induces fragmentation and restructuring of the inner membrane.
source: These observations indicate that, besides outer membrane ruptures, Bax activity induces fragmentation and restructuring of the inner membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on observations of inner membrane morphology in apoptotic mitochondria.

claim: In Bax/Bak DKO HCT116 cells stably expressing GFP-Bax induced with ABT-737, the signals of GFP-Bax foci localized to ribosome-exclusion zones like in HeLa cells overexpressing GFP-Bax.
source: We found that the signals of GFP-Bax foci localized to ribosome-exclusion zones like in HeLa cells overexpressing GFP-Bax (Figure 2—figure supplement 2G).
evidence: This is an observation from correlative microscopy of drug-induced apoptosis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: In drug-induced apoptosis in HCT116 cells, ruptured outer membranes were observed, mostly (3 of 5 ruptures) near Bax clusters.
source: We also observed ruptured outer membranes, mostly (3 of 5 ruptures) near Bax clusters.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from electron tomography of drug-induced apoptosis.

claim: Ruptures were less frequent in drug-induced apoptosis in HCT116 cells (5 ruptures for 45 GFP-Bax target signals) than in HeLa cells overexpressing Bax.
source: The ruptures were, however, less frequent (5 ruptures for 45 GFP-Bax target signals) than in HeLa cells.
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison between two experimental conditions.

claim: Ruptured mitochondria in drug-induced apoptosis displayed multiple matrices and unfolded inner membranes, similar to those in Bax-overexpressing HeLa cells.
source: These ruptured mitochondria displayed multiple matrices and unfolded inner membranes, similar to those in Bax-overexpressing HeLa cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–L).
evidence: This is an observation from electron tomography comparing two experimental conditions shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Ribosome-excluding Bax clusters, ruptures in the outer membrane, and rearrangements of the inner membrane are characteristic of Bax activity independent of means inducing apoptosis.
source: These results suggest that ribosome-excluding Bax clusters, ruptures in the outer membrane, as well as rearrangements of the inner membrane are characteristic of Bax activity independent of means inducing apoptosis.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of Bax overexpression and drug-induced apoptosis data.

claim: In electron cryo-tomograms of vitreous sections, ribosome-exclusion zones were found in the cytosol at predicted GFP-Bax locations (N = 7 GFP-Bax signals).
source: In electron cryo-tomograms acquired at the predicted GFP-Bax locations, we found ribosome-exclusion zones in the cytosol, in agreement with our data from resin-embedded cells (Figure 3C and G) (N = 7 GFP-Bax signals).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from cryo-ET of vitreous sections shown in Figure 3.

claim: Within ribosome-exclusion zones, irregularly arranged plane and line segments were discerned that appeared to be part of a dense network.
source: Within these exclusion zones, we could discern ultrastructural details that were not visible in the electron tomograms of resin-embedded cells (Figure 3D and H, and Videos 1 and 2). We found irregularly arranged plane and line segments that appeared to be part of a dense network within the exclusion zones that corresponded to GFP-Bax localization (Figure 3D' and H', and Videos 1 and 2; red highlights).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET of vitreous sections shown in Figure 3 and Videos 1 and 2.

claim: The number of detected segments was consistently higher in areas corresponding to GFP-Bax signals than in areas that did not correlate to GFP-Bax signals.
source: We consistently found that the number of detected segments was higher in areas corresponding to GFP-Bax signals than in the areas that did not correlate to GFP-Bax signals (Figure 3—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This is a quantitative analysis using ridge detection shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Bax clusters contain elements indicative of a higher order ultrastructural organization.
source: These data suggest that Bax clusters are not amorphous, featureless structures, but that they contain elements indicative of a higher order ultrastructural organization.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of structural features in Bax clusters by cryo-ET.

claim: Adjacent to outer mitochondrial membrane ruptures in three different cells, six ribosome-exclusion zones were found that contained similar structural motifs as observed in vitreous sections.
source: Adjacent to outer mitochondrial membrane ruptures in three different cells, we found six ribosome-exclusion zones that contained similar structural motifs as observed in vitreous sections.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from cryo-ET of cryo-FIB milled cells.

claim: The regions adjacent to ruptures contained small planar segments with an average length of 21 nm (SD 5.6 nm, N = 59 segments from 3 clusters from two different cells).
source: These regions contained small planar segments, which manifest as lines in individual tomographic slices. The segments appeared irregularly connected to each other in a network (Figure 3K', N' and Q', and Videos 3 and 4; red highlights). The average length of the segments was 21 nm (SD 5.6 nm, N = 59 segments from 3 clusters from two different cells).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from cryo-ET of cryo-FIB milled cells shown in Figure 3 and Videos 3 and 4.

claim: The network ultrastructure of Bax clusters resembled a sponge with irregular fenestration, containing patches of high or low density.
source: The network ultrastructure resembled a sponge with irregular fenestration, containing patches of high or low density.
evidence: This is a descriptive observation from cryo-ET data.

claim: Using two different vitrification and two independent imaging methods, structural motifs were identified that suggest Bax clusters contain higher order structures and their supramolecular organization resembles a sponge-like meshwork.
source: Thus, using two different vitrification and two independent imaging methods, we identify structural motifs that suggest that Bax clusters contain higher order structures and their supramolecular organization resembles a sponge-like meshwork.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on observations from multiple cryo-ET approaches.

claim: The ruptured membrane bilayers displayed distinct, often sharp edges that were similar in thickness to the rest of the membrane.
source: The ruptured membrane bilayers displayed distinct, often sharp edges (Figure 4D–I) that were similar in thickness to the rest of the membrane.
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Some of the rupture edges appeared embedded into the cluster.
source: Some of the rupture edges appeared embedded into the cluster (Figure 3K,N,Q and Figure 4F,H).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Fragments of bilayer that appeared continuous with the outer membrane appeared also connected to the cluster.
source: Furthermore, fragments of bilayer that appeared continuous with the outer membrane appeared also connected to the cluster (Figure 3Q; yellow arrowheads).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In 11 of the 12 outer membrane ruptures visualized by cryo-ET, the inner membrane appeared intact with no visible rupture.
source: In 11 of the 12 outer membrane ruptures we visualized by cryo-ET, the inner membrane appeared intact with no visible rupture.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from cryo-ET data.

claim: In one case, both outer and inner membranes were ruptured, and a Bax cluster was protruding through the rupture into the mitochondrial matrix.
source: In only one case, we observed that both outer and inner membranes were ruptured, and a Bax cluster was protruding through the rupture into the mitochondrial matrix (Figure 3O–Q').
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 3.

claim: In 11 cases of ruptured outer membrane, substantial segments of the inner membrane were exposed to the cytosol at the site of the rupture.
source: In the other 11 cases of ruptured outer membrane, substantial segments of the inner membrane were exposed to the cytosol at the site of the rupture (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 4.

claim: In nine cases of ruptured outer membrane, there were no cristae protruding from the exposed inner membrane segment, and no intracristae spaces exposed to the outer membrane ruptures.
source: In nine of these cases, there were no cristae protruding from the exposed inner membrane segment, and no intracristae spaces exposed to the outer membrane ruptures (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Exposed inner membrane segments appeared very smooth relative to the rest of the inner membrane, which displayed cristae of variable curvature that protruded into the matrix.
source: Thus, these segments appeared very smooth relative to the rest of the inner membrane, which displayed cristae of variable curvature that protruded into the matrix (Figure 4J–L).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 4.

claim: Ruptured mitochondria were classified into three categories based on inner membrane morphology: Lamellar, approximately parallel cristae (N = 9), multiple matrices (N = 14), and mostly unfolded or short, tubular cristae (N = 20).
source: We classified the ruptured mitochondria that we observed both by ET of resin-embedded cells and by cryo-ET of cryo-FIB milled HeLa cells, into three categories based on inner membrane morphology: Lamellar, approximately parallel cristae (N = 9), multiple matrices (N = 14), and mostly unfolded or short, tubular cristae (N = 20) (Figure 4M).
evidence: This is a classification and quantification of mitochondria from ET data shown in Figure 4M.

claim: The smallest rupture sizes of approximately 100 nm were observed in all three categories of inner membrane morphology.
source: While we observed the smallest rupture sizes of approximately 100 nm in all three categories, increasingly larger ruptures were found for mitochondria with multiple matrices and with unfolded cristae, respectively (Figure 4M, p=0.0024).
evidence: This is an observation from quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4M.

claim: Increasingly larger ruptures were found for mitochondria with multiple matrices and with unfolded cristae (p=0.0024).
source: While we observed the smallest rupture sizes of approximately 100 nm in all three categories, increasingly larger ruptures were found for mitochondria with multiple matrices and with unfolded cristae, respectively (Figure 4M, p=0.0024).
evidence: This is a statistically significant finding from quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4M.

claim: Rupture size and the degree of inner membrane reshaping correlate with each other.
source: These results indicate that rupture size and the degree of inner membrane reshaping correlate with each other.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the quantitative analysis of rupture sizes in different categories of inner membrane morphology.

claim: For mitochondria with unfolded cristae, the percentage of mitochondrial surface area that consisted of exposed inner membrane varied between 2% and 50% (mean total surface area: 1.15 µm2, SD 0.41 µm2, N = 19; mean surface area of exposed inner membrane: 0.21 µm2, SD 0.19 µm2, N = 19).
source: The percentage of mitochondrial surface area that consisted of exposed inner membrane varied between 2% and 50% (mean total surface area: 1.15 µm2, SD 0.41 µm2, N = 19; mean surface area of exposed inner membrane: 0.21 µm2, SD 0.19 µm2, N = 19) (Figure 4N).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from analysis of mitochondria with unfolded cristae shown in Figure 4N.

claim: Rupture sizes varied largely at a given stage of inner membrane remodeling.
source: Thus, rupture sizes varied largely at a given stage of inner membrane remodeling.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the variability observed in the quantitative analysis.

claim: Mitochondria with unfolded inner membranes did not appear different in density than the surrounding cytosol in cryo-ET.
source: However, in our data set the mitochondria with unfolded inner membranes did not appear different in density than the surrounding cytosol (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The ratio of average matrix-gray value to cytosol-gray value was close to one in cells overexpressing GFP-Bax (N = 4 mitochondria).
source: To assess this observation quantitatively, we measured the ratio of average matrix-gray value to cytosol-gray value in electron cryo-tomograms of HeLa cells overexpressing GFP-Bax (Figure 5A) (N = 4 mitochondria). For comparison, we acquired electron cryo-tomograms of mitochondria in control HeLa cells that did not overexpress Bax and performed the same measurement (Figure 5B) (N = 5 mitochondria). The ratio was close to one in the cells overexpressing GFP-Bax, suggesting that the matrices of these mitochondria were similar in macromolecular density to the cytosol (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5.

claim: In mitochondria of control cells, the ratio of average matrix-gray value to cytosol-gray value was significantly lower than in Bax-overexpressing cells (p<0.0001).
source: In mitochondria of control cells, the ratio was significantly lower (Figure 5C, p<0.0001), as expected for a compartment higher in macromolecular density than the cytosol.
evidence: This is a statistically significant finding from quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Mitochondria that had unfolded inner membranes in Bax-overexpressing cells had dilute matrices as compared to mitochondria in control cells.
source: These results indicate that the mitochondria that had unfolded inner membranes in Bax-overexpressing cells had dilute matrices as compared to mitochondria in control cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the quantitative analysis of matrix density.

claim: ATP synthase heads were recognizable in the dilute matrices of apoptotic mitochondria.
source: The dilute matrices allowed us to see individual protein complexes within the mitochondria of Bax-overexpressing HeLa cells, usually obscured by the high protein density (Kühlbrandt, 2015). In particular, ATP synthase heads were recognizable.
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data, with citation to previous work on mitochondrial protein density.

claim: ATP synthases were abundant on cristae in apoptotic mitochondria.
source: ATP synthases were abundant on cristae (Figure 5F and F'; matching arrowheads).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5.

claim: ATP synthases were present on shallow indentations of the boundary membrane, albeit more rarely than on cristae.
source: Albeit more rarely, ATP synthases were also present on shallow indentations of the boundary membrane, the region of the inner membrane directly opposed to the outer membrane (Figure 5G and G'; arrowheads).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5.

claim: No ATP synthase heads were observed on the smooth regions of the inner membrane exposed to the cytosol by the ruptured outer membrane.
source: No ATP synthase heads were observed on the smooth regions of the inner membrane exposed to the cytosol by the ruptured outer membrane (Figure 5H and H').
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The frequency of observing ATP synthases appeared to correlate with membrane curvature and the localization seemed to require an intact, adjacent outer membrane.
source: Thus, the frequency of observing ATP synthases appeared to correlate with membrane curvature and the localization seemed to require an intact, adjacent outer membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on observations of ATP synthase distribution in different membrane regions.

claim: On cristae, the average angle enclosed by ATP synthase dimer heads and the membrane between them was 106˚ (SD 19˚, N = 81 dimers).
source: On cristae, dimers were readily discernable (Figure 5F). Within these dimers, we measured the angle enclosed by the two heads and the membrane between the two monomers (Figure 5I). The average angle was 106˚ (SD 19˚, N = 81 dimers)(Figure 5J).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5.

claim: 106˚ measured between ATP synthase heads and membrane correspond to approximately 70˚ between the major stalks.
source: Note that 106˚ measured in this way correspond to approximately 70˚ between the major stalks.
evidence: This is an explanation of the measurement method and its relationship to known ATP synthase structure.

claim: For ATP synthases on boundary membranes, the average angle between neighboring ATP synthases was 53˚ (SD 15˚), measured for 66 angles between 52 ATP synthases.
source: On the boundary membrane it was not possible to unambiguously identify dimers among ATP synthases (Figure 5G). We therefore measured all possible angles between neighboring ATP synthases. These measurements thus included potential dimers as well as monomers positioned near to each other. For 52 ATP synthases on boundary membranes, we measured 66 angles between ATP synthase pairs (Figure 5J). The average angle was 53˚ (SD 15˚), and only three ATP synthase pairs enclosed angles within the range we had measured for dimers in cristae, indicating that the majority of ATP synthases on the boundary membrane were not arranged into dimers similar to those on cristae.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Only three ATP synthase pairs on boundary membranes enclosed angles within the range measured for dimers in cristae, indicating that the majority of ATP synthases on the boundary membrane were not arranged into dimers similar to those on cristae.
source: The average angle was 53˚ (SD 15˚), and only three ATP synthase pairs enclosed angles within the range we had measured for dimers in cristae, indicating that the majority of ATP synthases on the boundary membrane were not arranged into dimers similar to those on cristae.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on quantitative analysis of ATP synthase angles.

claim: Bax-mediated flattening of the inner membrane is coupled to changes in the supramolecular organization of ATP synthases.
source: These results suggest that Bax-mediated flattening of the inner membrane is coupled to changes in the supramolecular organization of ATP synthases.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on observations of ATP synthase organization in different membrane regions.

claim: Changes in ATP synthase organization involve the dissociation of dimers into monomers upon unfolding of cristae, and clearance of ATP synthase heads from areas of smooth, cytosol-exposed inner membrane segments.
source: These changes involve the dissociation of dimers into monomers upon unfolding of cristae, and clearance of ATP synthase heads from areas of smooth, cytosol-exposed inner membrane segments.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on observations of ATP synthase distribution and organization.

claim: In correlative microscopy data from resin-embedded apoptotic Bax/Bak DKO HCT116 cells, MitoTracker signals localized to clumps of electron-dense compartments that were adjacent to GFP-Bax spots.
source: Recently, leakage of mtDNA into the cytosol of apoptotic cells was reported to result from expulsion of inner membrane compartments through ruptured outer membranes (McArthur et al., 2018). In our correlative microscopy data from resin-embedded apoptotic Bax/Bak DKO HCT116 cells stably expressing GFP-Bax, MitoTracker signals localized to clumps of electron-dense compartments that were adjacent to GFP-Bax spots (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This is an observation from correlative microscopy data shown in Figure 6, with citation to previous work on mtDNA leakage.

claim: In cryo-ET data of HCT116 cells, single-membrane bound compartments were found that contained granular structures similar to those in the mitochondrial matrix, and highly curved membranes lined with particles reminiscent of ATP synthases.
source: In cryo-ET data of these cells prepared by cryo-FIB milling, we also found single-membrane bound compartments that contained granular structures similar to those in the mitochondrial matrix (Figure 6E and Wolf et al., 2017), and highly curved membranes lined with particles reminiscent of ATP synthases (Figure 6E–I).
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 6, with citation to previous work on mitochondrial matrix structure.

claim: The average distance from the center of putative ATP synthase heads to the membrane was similar in compartments without outer membrane in HCT116 cells (12.02 nm, SD 1.69 nm, N = 65) and in mitochondria in HeLa cells (12.07 nm, SD 1.00 nm, N = 65).
source: We therefore measured the shortest distance from the center of the head to the membrane. The average distance was similar in both data sets (Figure 6J; HCT116: 12.02 nm, SD 1.69 nm, N = 65; HeLa: 12.07 nm, SD 1.00 nm, N = 65), and matched estimates from known ATP synthase structures (Hahn et al., 2016; Hahn et al., 2018; Srivastava et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from cryo-ET data shown in Figure 6J, with citations to known ATP synthase structures.

claim: The particles in single-membrane compartments were likely ATP synthases, and hence these compartments corresponded to mitochondrial inner membranes lacking an outer membrane.
source: We concluded that these particles were likely ATP synthases, and hence these compartments corresponded to mitochondrial inner membranes lacking an outer membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on comparison of particle measurements with known ATP synthase structures.

claim: Bax activity can result in complete removal of the outer membrane.
source: These results indicate that Bax activity can result in complete removal of the outer membrane.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation of inner membrane compartments without outer membrane.

claim: Cristae unfolding leading to flattening of the inner membrane could exert pressure onto the outer membrane, causing rupturing of locally destabilized outer membrane areas.
source: This suggests a mechanism by which the inner membrane rearrangements could contribute to rupture formation: As the inner membrane flattens, the mismatch between inner and outer membrane surface area exerts pressure onto the outer membrane. This pressure could cause rupturing of outer membrane areas that are locally destabilized, for instance through accumulation of membrane-inserted Bax (Westphal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the observed correlation between inner membrane flattening and rupture size, with citation to previous work on Bax membrane insertion.

claim: Further inner membrane flattening could widen initial ruptures.
source: Further inner membrane flattening could widen initial ruptures.
evidence: This is a speculative extension of the proposed mechanism.

claim: The mechanism of cristae unfolding exerting pressure on the outer membrane could in principle generate large ruptures without removal of lipids from the outer membrane.
source: This mechanism could in principle generate large ruptures without removal of lipids from the outer membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the proposed mechanism.

claim: In the proposed model, rupture size would depend on the number and surface area of cristae to be unfolded in a given mitochondrion.
source: In this model, the rupture size would depend on the number and surface area of cristae to be unfolded in a given mitochondrion.
evidence: This is a prediction of the proposed mechanism.

claim: Variability in rupture sizes could be caused by the amount of membrane-inserted, accumulated Bax molecules generating tension in the outer membrane.
source: This variability in rupture sizes could also be caused by additional factors potentially impacting rupture size. One such factor could be the amount of membrane-inserted, accumulated Bax molecules generating tension in the outer membrane (Westphal et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for observed variability, with citation to previous work on Bax-induced membrane tension.

claim: It is possible that Bax clusters contain additional components beyond Bax, potentially originating from the cytosol, the intermembrane space or the outer membrane.
source: While these data suggest that Bax is uniformly distributed within these clusters, it is possible that they contain additional components. These could be molecules originating from the cytosol, the intermembrane space or the outer membrane.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the composition of Bax clusters.

claim: The lipid bilayer edges of the ruptures often appeared embedded in the Bax cluster meshwork or connected to its structural features.
source: We found that Bax clusters have a higher order organization consisting of interconnected planes or discs arranged in an irregular manner, reminiscent of a sponge-like meshwork. The lipid bilayer edges of the ruptures often appeared embedded in this meshwork or connected to its structural features.
evidence: This is an observation from cryo-ET data.

claim: Some of the sharp edges within the Bax cluster meshwork resemble side views of membranes, suggesting that the clusters might contain patches of membrane.
source: Some of the sharp edges within the meshwork resemble side views of membranes, suggesting that the clusters might contain patches of membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations from cryo-ET data.

claim: Previous models proposed that Bax/Bak cluster activity involves generating membrane tension, which is released by remodeling the bilayer of the planar outer membrane into a non-lamellar lipid arrangement.
source: Previous models proposed that Bax/Bak cluster activity involves generating membrane tension, which is released by remodeling the bilayer of the planar outer membrane into a non-lamellar lipid arrangement (Nasu et al., 2016; Uren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a statement of previous models with citations.

claim: Membrane remodeling could be aided by membrane sculpting proteins such as N-BAR domain proteins.
source: This remodeling could be aided by membrane sculpting proteins such as N-BAR domain proteins (Gallop et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative statement with citation to previous work on N-BAR proteins.

claim: The N-BAR protein endophilin B1 interacts with Bax during apoptosis in cultured cells.
source: The N-BAR protein endophilin B1 interacts with Bax during apoptosis in cultured cells (Takahashi et al., 2005) and, also through interaction with Bax, causes vesiculation of liposomes in vitro (Etxebarria et al., 2009; Rostovtseva et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Endophilin B1 causes vesiculation of liposomes in vitro through interaction with Bax.
source: The N-BAR protein endophilin B1 interacts with Bax during apoptosis in cultured cells (Takahashi et al., 2005) and, also through interaction with Bax, causes vesiculation of liposomes in vitro (Etxebarria et al., 2009; Rostovtseva et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous in vitro studies.

claim: The related N-BAR protein endophilin A1 can generate interconnected tubular membrane networks.
source: Notably, the related N-BAR protein endophilin A1 can generate interconnected tubular membrane networks (Ayton et al., 2009; Simunovic et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Lipids such as cardiolipin and ceramides were attributed roles in supporting Bax activity.
source: Furthermore, lipids such as cardiolipin and ceramides were attributed roles in supporting Bax activity (Jain et al., 2017; Kuwana et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: The higher order meshwork observed for Bax clusters might be a result of Bax reshaping outer membrane patches from a lamellar topology into a non-lamellar bilayer network, similar to sponge-like lipid cubic phases.
source: Thus, we speculate that the higher order meshwork we observe for Bax clusters is a result of Bax reshaping outer membrane patches from a lamellar topology into a non-lamellar bilayer network, similar to sponge-like lipid cubic phases (Valldeperas et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative model based on the observed structure of Bax clusters, with citation to work on lipid cubic phases.

claim: The model of Bax reshaping membrane into a meshwork would suggest that ruptures might be formed through removal of lipids from the outer membrane.
source: This model would suggest that ruptures might be formed through removal of lipids from the outer membrane.
evidence: This is a prediction of the speculative model.

claim: The model of Bax reshaping membrane would explain how clusters form: Bax might progressively deform the membrane into a meshwork-like structure, which grows as more Bax molecules accumulate and serves as a sink for outer membrane components.
source: It would additionally explain how the clusters form: Bax oligomerization requires the interaction with membranes (Bleicken et al., 2010), while clusters occupy a volume in the cytosol. Therefore, there must be a transition from accumulation of Bax molecules in the membrane plane to a three-dimensional cluster consisting of Bax molecules and potentially other components. Following association within the outer membrane, Bax might progressively deform the membrane into a meshwork-like structure, which grows as more Bax molecules accumulate and serves as a sink for outer membrane components (Uren et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative mechanism with citations to previous work on Bax oligomerization and cluster formation.

claim: The formation of the wide range of rupture sizes might be a consequence of two mechanisms: Cristae unfolding leading to flattening of the inner membrane, and sequestration of outer membrane components into Bax clusters.
source: Thus, the formation of the wide range of rupture sizes observed by others and us might be a consequence of two mechanisms: Cristae unfolding leading to flattening of the inner membrane, and sequestration of outer membrane components into Bax clusters (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a proposed comprehensive model based on the study's findings, shown in Figure 7.

claim: Ruptures allow influx of ribosomes and thus mixing of cytosolic and intermembrane content.
source: Ruptures allow influx of ribosomes and thus mixing of cytosolic and intermembrane content.
evidence: This is based on the observation of ribosomes in the intermembrane space.

claim: As rupture size increases, the inner membrane remodels through fragmentation and cristae unfolding.
source: As rupture size increases, the inner membrane remodels through fragmentation and cristae unfolding.
evidence: This is based on the observed correlation between rupture size and inner membrane morphology.

claim: Dilution of the mitochondrial matrix likely supports dilation of the inner membrane compartment.
source: Dilution of the mitochondrial matrix likely supports dilation of the inner membrane compartment.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed matrix dilution.

claim: Inner membrane reshaping is accompanied by disassembly of ATP synthase dimers into monomers and a complete clearance of ATP synthases from regions of inner membrane that are exposed to the cytosol and maximally flattened.
source: Inner membrane reshaping is accompanied by disassembly of ATP synthase dimers into monomers and a complete clearance of ATP synthases from regions of inner membrane that are exposed to the cytosol, and that are maximally flattened.
evidence: This is based on observations of ATP synthase distribution and organization in apoptotic mitochondria.

claim: The degree of inner membrane exposure varies, and is maximal in HCT116 cells, where inner membrane compartments devoid of any outer membrane can be found.
source: The degree of inner membrane exposure varies, and is maximal in HCT116 cells, where inner membrane compartments devoid of any outer membrane can be found.
evidence: This is based on observations comparing HeLa and HCT116 cells.
